svg.title: Initiative costing decision cycle
svg.desc: Eight numbered stations form a clockwise costing route. At every station, a decision question leads down to a costing method and then to a decision-ready output. A semantic table beside the visual carries the full working detail.

g.title: Initiative costing questions and clockwise route
g.text: Move clockwise across eight decision routes; inside each station, read question → method → output.
Q ↓ M ↓ O at every station

g.title: Clockwise route connecting all eight stations
Route 1. Where does the money go? Bottom-up resource-loaded work breakdown. Base estimate and staffing shape.
Route 2. What could move the commitment? Risk-register reserve plus sensitivity. Separate reserve plus movement drivers.
Route 3. What range should the sponsor carry? Ranged commitment model. Planning band and tail drivers.
Route 4. Which route has the strongest whole-system economics? Three-branch comparative total cost. Buy, build, or hybrid on one basis.
g.text: Buy / build / hybrid on one basis

g.title: Route 5. What does the capability cost across its useful life? Whole-life total cost plus operations and scale. Lifecycle total plus annual run curve.
Route 6. What does each sample, inspection, or transaction cost? Activity-based unit economics. Unit cost and volume curve.
Route 7. What does the current state cost, and what value can return? Status quo plus benefit realization. Priced baseline plus realized-value path.

text.tspan: What does the current state cost,

g.title: Route 8. What must a committee decide? Executive one-page business case. Basis, ask, timing, and consequences.
Shared decision record at the center
Costing doctrine
g.text: Every output travels with its basis, horizon, reserve, comparison baseline, date, and next decision.
